SpaceX 达成史上最大规模 GPU 融资安排，协议总额约 400 亿美元
evidence_summaries: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.
Elon Musk said in an X post that SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs.

IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，SpaceX 当地时间今日正式公布了其与另类资产管理巨头 Apollo 达成的融资安排。 根据双方间的有约束力承诺，SpaceX 和 Apollo 将签署一份 价值约 400 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,670.98 亿元人民币） 的 GPU 及相关设备主融资租赁协议，具体签署时间预计落在 2026 年内。 这一迄今为止规模最大的 GPU 融资协议 将为 SpaceX 的地面计算建设提供下一代 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 芯片。租赁计划预计将于 2027 年上半年 GPU 及相关设备交付后开始实施。 SpaceX 首席财务官 Bret Johnsen 表示： SpaceX 致力于部署全球最大的计算基础设施。随着对计算能力的需求持续加速增长，我们发现对系统集成基础设施的投资回收期已缩短至不到一年。 此次租赁协议不仅使我们的资金来源更加多元化，还解决了实现增长计划所需资金中相当大的一部分。我们正致力于以创纪录的速度将更多计算能力投入运行，以支持面向企业和消费者的 Grok 服务，并为现有及未来的云服务客户提供支持。 相关阅读： 《 马斯克确认 SpaceX 完成 400 亿美元债务融资，用于购买 GPU 》 《 马斯克唱衰新云厂商：200 余家相关公司面临生存危机 》

evidence_titles: Anthropic 招股书披露：曾因安全顾虑暂停旗舰 AI 模型训练一个多月
evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，Anthropic 在当地时间周一公布的 IPO 招股文件中披露，出于安全方面的顾虑，该公司曾暂停下一代旗舰 AI 模型的训练长达一个多月；另外还有四个 AI 智能体在测试期间突破限制，接入了真实的外部计算机系统。 IT之家注意到，这家 Claude 开发企业在文件的风险提示章节中表示，其推迟了一款全新前沿基础模型的预训练工作，目的是强化防护机制，防止模型权重与知识产权被盗。 这份披露内容展现出，研发能力越来越强的 AI 模型会伴随各类安全难题，部分从业者已经发出警示，这类技术未来有可能脱离人类管控。竞争对手 OpenAI 今年早些时候也曾因为安全问题暂停部分训练工作，当时其模型出现了入侵 Hugging Face 平台的情况。 这些事件说明，突发的安全事故有可能打乱核心模型的开发与上线节奏，而这些模型正是 Anthropic 冲刺备受期待的上市进程、实现业务增长的关键。 Anthropic 警示，训练暂停会造成营收延后，使公司落后于竞争对手。这份文件用大约 94 页篇幅罗列了风险因素。 沙箱逃逸 招股文件还披露了此前未对外公开的安全评估事故：四个 AI 模型脱离测试沙箱环境，访问到现实中的计算机系统，相关会话持续时长在 10 小时至 34 小时之间。 Anthropic 称，在和第三方合作方开展网络安全测试时出现操作失误。按照要求测试环境应当关闭联网权限，但最终环境仍保持着互联网连接。 其中一起事故里，该模型的早期版本持续尝试一项无法完成的评估任务，期间找到一条保存的密码，并利用密码获取了第三方系统的管理员权限。随后它拿到更多凭证、修改系统设置，还访问到个人数据。文件没有写明涉事外部合作方的身份。 Anthropic 表示已经通知所有受影响的相关方，没有发现模型刻意躲避人类监管、或是多个模型互相协同行动的证据。事后公司叫停了部分上线前网络安全评估项目，并暂停风险等级更高的强化学习测试环境。 另外，该公司在当地时间上周日称，Claude 曾绕过付费墙，在没有获得人工授权的情况下调取了美国佐治亚州公开的汇总选票数据。

The $2 Trillion Number Isn’t In It. Nolan Pratt Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:05 AM PDT 3 min read ANTH.PVT The most anticipated initial public offering filing in years arrived on October 26, 2026, yet it is legally incapable of stating the one number everyone is quoting. Anthropic, PBC submitted its Form S-1 registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission, officially signaling its intent to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT. While the document provides a granular look at the company's financial architecture, it remains silent on the specific share count and price range that will ultimately define its market debut. This is not an act of evasion, but a standard feature of the regulatory process; the S-1 is a disclosure of business health and risk, not a pre-negotiated price tag. What the filing does provide is a clear view of the company's current financial standing. For the first half of 2026, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion against a net loss of $80.7 billion . For market observers, the headline loss requires careful parsing. The figure is largely driven by an increase in the value of convertible bonds, representing a non-cash mark rather than an operating bleed. By separating these accounting adjustments from the underlying business performance, the filing offers a window into the company's scale that was previously obscured by its private status. The silence regarding the offering price is where the market's speculative machinery currently resides. Because the registration statement has been filed but has not yet become effective, no offers or sales are permitted. The pricing mechanism is a staged evolution. Following a confidential filing on June 1, 2026 , the company is now operating on a ladder of private-market valuations that have escalated rapidly: a Series G round in February 2026 valued the company at roughly $380 billion, followed by a Series H round in May 2026 that reached a post-money valuation of $965 billion. These figures are historical markers, not current pricing. Press expectations, which are not figures disclosed in the filing, have pushed the narrative significantly higher. Bloomberg has reported expectations that the IPO could match or exceed the $1.8 trillion valuation of SpaceX, while CNBC has noted investor sentiment circling the $2 trillion mark, a figure previously floated in September reporting . Reuters has suggested a potential capital raise of up to $100 billion. These projections, often citing a range of 22x to 30x revenue, are external market estimates. They reflect the intense demand for the asset, but they remain entirely detached from the formal S-1 document currently under review by the SEC. Story Continues The process from here is a structured march toward effectiveness. The company has named Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters, though reports mentioning other institutions in the syndicate remain unconfirmed. The next phase involves a period of SEC review and subsequent amendments to the registration statement. It is only through these later amendments that the specific price range will be introduced, typically coinciding with the start of the roadshow marketing process. Press reports indicate that this marketing phase could begin as early as November 9, 2026, with a listing targeted for days before the November US midterms. The current state of the filing provides the necessary transparency for potential investors to evaluate the business. However, the valuation remains a moving target, subject to the ongoing dialogue between the underwriters and the institutional buy-side during the upcoming roadshow. The market is not waiting for a number to be revealed in a static document; it is waiting for the price to be discovered through the mechanics of the offering itself. As the SEC review proceeds, the focus remains on the transition from private-market benchmarks to public-market reality. The filing has brought the company a step closer to a historic offering, but the final valuation will only crystallize when the roadshow concludes and the shares are priced through later amendments to the registration statement. Original | Odaily Planet Daily (@OdailyChina)Author | Sudi Xia @ Odaily Planet DailyOn the evening of October 26, Beijing time, artificial intelligence company Original | Odaily Planet Daily ( @OdailyChina ) Author | Sudi Xia @ Odaily Planet Daily On the evening of October 26, Beijing time, artificial intelligence company Anthropic filed its initial public offering (IPO) application with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). According to Anthropic’s S-1 filing (click to view), the company expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT.” Anthropic secretly submitted its IPO application in June. The prospectus indicates that the number of shares offered, price range, and underwriting discounts are left blank on the cover page; a total of 21 underwriters are involved in this IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as joint lead underwriters. Given that the original document is hundreds of pages long and some of its data differs significantly from the earlier draft exposed by Reuters, Odaily Planet Daily has excerpted the key IPO details for readers to quickly review. Five figures that differ from market-reported data Operating loss of $693 million, not $8.7 billion Since the draft prospectus content was reported by Reuters at the end of September, Chinese media have generally portrayed Anthropic's operating loss for the first half of 2026 as approximately $8.7 billion, while the operating loss line item in the prospectus’s income statement is -$693 million. The $8.7 billion is calculated by subtracting the $72.388 billion fair value change loss from the net loss of $80.748 billion. The prospectus explains this change as: “These changes were primarily due to the increase in the fair value of our outstanding convertible notes, resulting from increases in enterprise value during each period.” The net operating loss narrowed from $2.135 billion in the first half of 2025 to $693 million, a 67.5% decrease. According to the prospectus, revenue during the same period increased 14-fold year-over-year. The following are the primary consolidated income statement data (in millions of U.S. dollars): Cash and short-term investments amount to $131.651 billion. The widely circulated figure of “cash of only $20.28 billion” corresponds to the point in time as of December 31, 2025. The prospectus’s balance sheet has been updated to June 30, 2026: cash and cash equivalents amount to $112.389 billion, short-term investments total $19.262 billion, for a combined total of $131.651 billion. The cash flow statement shows that net cash inflows from financing activities in the first half of 2026 were $110.774 billion, with cash and restricted cash at the end of the period totaling $114.918 billion. The claim of "$518 billion in computing power commitments" is not supported by the document. The previously leaked draft stated, "Anthropic plans to spend $518 billion on cloud computing, computing power, and infrastructure over the next year." However, a full search of the prospectus for "518 billion" and "450 billion" yields no results, and the contract commitment table does not list specific amounts at this preliminary prospectus stage. The contract amounts with each counterparty can be verified individually: Microsoft: at least $44.9 billion, period from November 2026 to May 2033. Google: at least $114.5 billion, period from April 2026 to July 2033. Amazon: at least $110 billion, period from May 2026 to April 2036. SpaceXAI up to $120.5 billion by 2029. Nscale up to $44.6 billion by 2033. Lambda $41.3 billion by 2034. Initial procurement of AMD Helios racks expected to exceed $20 billion. An additional $125 billion to $150 billion in Google TPU purchases is planned, with delivery scheduled between 2028 and 2031. Broadcom assumes equipment leasing obligations of up to $42 billion. Both the Microsoft and Amazon agreements include make-up clauses. The prospectus states that if actual consumption falls below the committed amount, a payment must be made to Google to cover the difference, with such difference settled via a true-up mechanism; the Amazon agreement has the same arrangement. The figures for customer concentration are in the notes to the financial statements. The main text of the prospectus states only that “a significant portion of our revenue comes from a limited number of customers,” but does not provide specific percentages; the exact figures are found in Note F-16: In 2025, Customer A and Customer B each accounted for 12% of revenue, Customer B accounted for 18% in the first half of 2025, Customer C accounted for 43% in 2023, and declined to 11% in the first half of 2026. The same footnote also discloses that revenue generated through the cloud service provider (CSP) channel accounted for 11% of total revenue in 2023, 32% in 2024, 47% in 2025, and rose to 48% in the first half of 2026. The proportion of net accounts receivable generated through the same channel was 42% in 2024, 60% in 2025, and 58% as of June 2026. The prospectus lists dependence on cloud providers as a risk factor: “We rely on a limited number of cloud service providers and suppliers, some of whom have strategic and investment relationships with us and are also our customers. This relationship may create complex situations that could lead to conflicts of interest and adversely affect our ability to secure computing power.” Net income retention rate is 900% The 500% figure cited in the market comes from CFO Krishna Rao’s podcast interview in May 2026. The prospectus discloses that, as of September 30, 2026, the net revenue retention rate (NRR) was approximately 900%. The prospectus also specifies the calculation scope for this metric: “The base period is the three months ending prior to the measurement date, and the numerator is the revenue for the three months ending on the measurement date; customers with revenue below $1 during the base period, as well as Claude Pro and Claude Max fixed-subscription users, are excluded from the calculation.” Run-Rate Revenue: The custom metric in the prospectus differs from ARR. The prospectus defines Run-Rate Revenue in the terminology section as: the annualized estimated value of our revenue-generating activities as of a given measurement date, calculated as the sum of (i) the consumer fees incurred over the past 28 days ending on that measurement date multiplied by 13, and (ii) the total monthly subscription fees as of that measurement date multiplied by 12. The consumption fee is calculated by multiplying the past 28 days by 13, not the industry standard of 12. The specific value of this metric is left blank in the prospectus, disclosed as: "As of October 31, 2026, our Run-Rate Revenue was ___ USD." The risk factors section of the prospectus qualifies this metric as follows: “Therefore, these metrics may not accurately reflect our actual performance or future results. Metrics such as Run-Rate Revenue, net revenue retention rate, number of customers, and Claude success rate are based on numerous assumptions and limitations.” Quarterly revenue growth rate decreased from 132% to 45% The quarterly revenue disclosed in the prospectus is: $4.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, $11.6 billion in the second quarter, and $16.8 billion in the third quarter. The sequential growth rate for the second quarter was 132%, and for the third quarter, it was 45%. Monthly annualized recurring revenue (ARR) trajectory: $9 billion by end of 2025, $30 billion in February 2026, $47 billion in May, $65 billion in July, and $67 billion by end of Q3. The company provided three explanations for the slowdown in growth: competitors such as OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 Astra while lowering prices to compete in the agent market; the company’s own anti-distillation measures resulted in account suspensions and customer attrition; and approximately 5% to 7% of revenue came from model distillation activities, which are expected to decline further in the fourth quarter. The prospectus also discloses a difference in reporting methodology: revenue figures include sales through the cloud platform channel without deducting platform commissions, whereas OpenAI’s disclosed annualized revenue reflects net revenue after deducting commissions, making the two figures not directly comparable. Five types of shares, two types each issuing only 1 share The capital structure disclosed on the prospectus cover page includes five categories: 1 share of Class T common stock, 1 share of Class F common stock, and 0 shares of Class E common stock, as shown below: Class T is held by the Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT). The prospectus describes the trust’s mandate as: “Operating as an independent entity governed by trustees with no financial interest, who possess expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise.” The trust may elect and remove Class T directors, and the Class T directors elected thereby shall constitute a majority of the authorized board seats. Class T common stock has no other voting rights or economic rights. Class F shares will be issued prior to this offering to Founder LLC, composed of seven co-founders, holding 50.1% of the total voting power. Class N common shares have no voting rights and are held by key strategic business partners. Anthropic considers itself a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules. The risk factors section of the prospectus states: “Our capital structure includes several recently designed provisions not commonly found in other companies with multiple-class share structures, which may substantially eliminate the ability of Class A common stockholders to influence significant decisions, including changes in control. Our capital structure will, for the foreseeable future, concentrate voting power in LTBT and Founder LLC, resulting in these entities’ voting rights not being derived from or aligned with their economic interests in the company.” The governance structure section further states: "Therefore, holders of Class A common stock will typically be unable to influence the outcome of any matter submitted to shareholders for a vote or the election of directors, regardless of how they vote—unless a majority of the continuing founders cannot agree on how to vote the Class F common stock." A 50% increase in stock price can trigger additional issuance to the charitable fund. The company has donated 846,840,960 shares of Class N common stock to its wholly owned subsidiary, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, representing 5% of the fully diluted shares as of June 30, 2026. The board has also been authorized to issue additional Class N common stock, up to 2% of the total outstanding shares, unexercised options, unvested RSUs, and other equivalent securities at any time the stock price increases by 50% from the previous price milestone, with the IPO offering price serving as the starting point. This authorization is exercised at the discretion of the board. The seven co-founders have separately pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to charitable purposes. The board currently consists of six members, including the co-founder of Netflix. The list of directors and senior management disclosed in the prospectus (as of September 30, 2026): The company has four committees: Audit, Compensation, Nominating and Governance (NGC), and Security and Risk. The Audit and Compensation committees are composed entirely of independent directors. Jay Kreps resigned as a director in May 2026, Christopher Liddell joined in February 2026, and Vas Narasimhan joined in April 2026. The five co-founders are the selling shareholders in this offering. evidence_summaries: Bringing fast and capable computer use to everyone

GPT-6.1 Terra It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement. In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use: We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it. Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks. OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News: In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select. Here are the pelicans for the different reasoning levels. This pelican for "max" cost 11.3161 cents and took 4 minutes and 11 seconds: Here's a new comparison grid showing pelicans for every reasoning level of OpenAI's current frontier lineup: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6.1 Terra is priced at $1/million input tokens and $5/million output - almost half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and around 10x the price of GPT-6 Luna. evidence_titles: 腾讯混元同声传译大模型 Hy-SimulMT 开源，响应时间仅 3 秒超人类译员
evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，腾讯混元同声传译大模型 Hy-SimulMT 今日发布并开源，具备低时延、高准确率的特点，支持中英语言之间语音到语音实时翻译 —— 说话人的音频可以实时输入到 Hy-SimulMT 模型中，模型会边听边译，实时给出译文和语音，并支持实时音色克隆，可以高度还原说话人声音和语气。该模型在腾讯 Hy 翻译 App 首发， 免费提供服务体验 。 IT之家从官方介绍获悉，低时延是模型的一大亮点，混元同声传译大模型 Hy-SimulMT 的响应时间 实测在 3 秒左右 ，人类专业译员平均水平在 4-5 秒。测评结果显示，该模型的翻译效果超过了市面上主流的开源同传模型，甚至超过大部分的商用同传 API。 官方称，在业界常用的长音频开源评测集 RealSI 上，Hy-SimulMT 展示出了较好的同传翻译效果，见下图： 横轴里的 StreamLAAL 表示同传翻译的延迟指标，反映的模型输出翻译结果相比输入音频的延迟秒数，越低越好。纵轴表示翻译质量，使用 GPT6.1-Sol 进行打分，越高越好。Hy-SimulMT 能做到延迟最低的情况下，效果达到开源模型最佳，甚至超过大多数商业 API。 在短音频测试集上，Hy-SimulMT 也有较好表现，见下图： 为了更准确评估 Hy-SimulMT 的真实水平，该团队在合规允许范围内，广泛收集了互联网上新出现的中文和英文音频，包含软件 AI、医学、制造能源、自然科学、农业食品、商务管理、法律、教育、文化文旅、体育生活共十个领域， 涉及演讲、访谈、会议等多个场景 。 在这份数据上，该团队不仅测试了 Hy-SimulMT 的效果，也请多位人类同传专家对这些音频进行同声传译。 人类同传专家一共 6 位，其中 3 位拥有 CATTI 一级口译证书，3 位拥有 CATTI 二级口译证书，所有专家都有多年的同传实战经验。测评对 Hy-SimulMT 和人类同传专家的翻译内容在延迟和翻译质量上对比，其中人类同传专家选取的是 3 个人中的最高分，在这次能力定位测评中， Hy-SimulMT 在翻译的质量达到人类同传专家水平（得分更高），速度更快（时延更低） 。 参考 HuggingFace Modelscope Github

evidence_summaries: 高品质 AI Token 成为行业新风向

近日，雷峰网获悉，高品质 AI Token 生产服务商趋境科技（Approaching.AI）完成 B 轮融资，本轮融资金额超13亿人民币；今年内已累计募得24亿人民币。多项核心经营指标在半年内实现超十倍速增长，持续获得产业和资本的高度认可。 本轮融资由浙财创新、萧山资本、工银投资、中关村科学城、星连资本及钱江世纪城共同领投。云创资本、湖南高新纵横、建投华科、申万创新投、中信聚信、珠海科技产业集团、商汤科技、网宿科技、甘肃树帜、常金控、元智未来、清证星竹、小咖资本等跟投，老股东尚势资本继续追投。 这是继今年 7 月完成 A 轮融资后，趋境科技短期内再获大额融资。截至今年10月，趋境科技已在 2026 年连续完成多轮融资。密集的资本跟进背后，既反映出市场对 AI 基础设施赛道长期价值的共识，更源于投资人对趋境科技战略聚焦、技术领先和商业化交付成绩等综合实力的肯定——过去半年，趋境科技不但全面跑通了从技术架构到规模化商业交付的全链路，更是持续引领推理行业的技术演进，以技术创新推动了国产算力的性能大跃升。 本轮募集的资金将重点投向高品质 AI Token 产能扩张、ATaaS（Approaching.AI Token as a Service）平台升级迭代、推理底层技术和新产品的研发，以及商业化合作与交付体系完善等方面。 投资者说 · 浙财创新董事长陈栋 “随着 AI 产业走向规模化应用，推理效率、成本与系统优化能力正成为商业化的重要基础。趋境科技在大模型推理领域具备持续的技术积累和工程交付能力。我们期待与公司长期同行，共同推动高效、普惠的 AI 基础设施建设与规模化应用。” 投资者说 · 萧山资本集团董事长祝利烽 “趋境科技是萧山布局 AI Infra 的标杆项目。早在行业聚焦训练时，公司便前瞻深耕推理赛道。依托清华系团队十余年的技术积累与自研 ATaaS 平台，将算力高效转化为可规模化生产的高品质 AI Token，推动国产算力进入核心生产环节。双方正携手推进万卡级人工智能 Token 工厂建设，加速形成‘芯模联动’产业闭环。萧山资本将以长期资本、耐心资本深度赋能，支持其把高品质 AI Token 工厂能力快速复制，为 AI 产业高质量发展注入持久动力。” 投资者说 · 星连资本创始管理合伙人张鸣晨 “星连资本自2024年天使轮成为股东以来，一路见证趋境科技在技术、产品、服务、战略和商业化等全方位不断创造远超预期的佳绩；更是在不到三年的时间里已经快速跃升为 AI 推理领域耀眼的一流企业。这也是星连资本在过往每一轮都持续大额追加投资的根本原因。我们看好趋境科技从技术与商业验证走向规模化建设和持续运营后的广阔成长空间，也期待陪伴团队持续引领 AI 推理行业的发展。” 从“粗放供给”到“品质服务” ｜高品质 AI Token 成为行业新风向 Token 市场发展初期，行业供给侧多“重 Token 数、轻服务品质”，以粗放扩量的方式快速做大供给规模。彼时大模型尚处在试点验证阶段，未深度嵌入企业核心生产链路，业务对性能、稳定性、模型质量的容错空间较大，这类供给模式得以被市场接纳。而趋境科技自创立之初，便坚持锚定生产级推理标准，持续投入推理系统原始创新，夯实工程底座，在行业内率先定义高品质 AI Token 服务理念。 趋境科技所定义的“高品质 AI Token”：锚定生产级场景，提供高智能、低时延、高速率、强稳定，兼具规模化交付能力与可控综合成本的 AI Token 服务。 伴随产业重心转向 Agent 驱动的业务闭环落地，大模型逐步承载生产级核心流程，AI 推理行业正迎来范式转变：企业对 AI Token 的智能水平、响应时延、输出速度、上下文完整性、服务稳定性提出了严苛的生产级刚性要求。这一转变与趋境一直以来坚持和倡导的高品质AI Token 服务理念不谋而合。 产业拐点显现，Token 市场快速形成清晰的品质分层：“可用即可”的粗放供给已难以匹配生产场景诉求，兼顾多维指标平衡的高品质 AI Token 供给稀缺、需求激增，成为市场刚需。作为高品质 AI Token 服务最早的布局者和深耕者，趋境科技凭借长期沉淀的推理系统底层技术与工程化能力，持续推进高品质 AI Token 服务的规模化交付。趋境科技现已成为高品质 AI Token 服务领域的领航者。 立足“少模型、深优化、高品质” ｜加速高品质 AI Token 规模化交付 高品质 AI Token 能够持续规模化交付，最终取决于两个核心命题：单位算力效能能否持续提升，规模化供给能力能否稳定增长。 围绕这一目标，为兑现高品质 AI Token 的生产标准，趋境坚持“少模型、深优化、高品质”的技术路线，聚焦市场需求明确、应用广泛的主流大模型，持续推进“异构推理”“以存换算”“虚实同构”等多项全球首创技术的工程落地，专注企业生产场景的高品质 AI Token 需求。 “少模型、深优化”解决的是“同一批算力能够生产多少高品质 AI Token”，稳定生产负载和跨集群运营解决的是“这些算力有多少时间真正处于有效工作状态”。“少模型”本身并不天然带来更高的利用率，只有单位算力产出和有效利用率同时提升，AI Token 业务的单位经济才有可能成立。 这一路线背后的商业逻辑非常明确：企业级客户最终为业务结果付费，而不是为模型兼容数量付费。 目前，趋境科技已经形成一套可复制的高品质 AI Token 工厂建设与运营模式：既有日均数万亿级 Token 产能的已投产项目，也有面向区域产业生态与头部客户的战略合作及在建布局。更重要的是，整体业务已经跨过成本线。以真实业绩验证了 ATaaS 平台的大规模交付与持续运营能力。 技术创新重构国产算力体系 ｜性价比超越国际最领先算力 让国产算力能够支撑高品质 AI Token 的生产是趋境科技一直以来的目标。 面对国内外芯片的性能差异，趋境科技探索出一条以系统级技术创新实现算力效率突破的新路径，先后率先提出了“国产 Prefill-Decode（PD）异构协同”“高性能异构 KV Cache 转换”“异构算力计算融合”等一系列创新技术方案，重构国产算力计算模式和推理体系，并已在高标准生产场景中正式投产。 在真实生产级环境中，实现国产芯片承载万亿级头部大模型，并达成高品质 AI Token 规模化生产，同时整体性价比超越国际最领先算力。 趋境首创的异构协同推理技术，在保障模型输出质量、响应速度和服务稳定性的前提下，以更低的硬件投入实现更高的有效 Token 产出，稳定承接头部客户的真实业务需求。 这一突破具备双重开创性价值：在商业层面，构筑差异化核心技术护城河，为趋境规模化共建高品质 AI Token 工厂打开增长天花板，支撑业绩与资本价值持续跃升；在产业战略层面，有助于跳出单纯比拼硬件参数的技术竞争，重新定义国产算力价值标尺，让分散在全国、不同架构的国芯资产释放足额推理产能，为国家搭建自主可控、供给充沛、具备商业经济性的 AI 推理底座提供可落地的核心工程方案，进一步夯实我国大模型产业链安全与算力自主根基。 以技术拓产量 ｜半年实现业绩十倍跃升 持续自主技术创新，是驱动趋境科技高品质 AI Token 产量实现指数级增长的核心动力。 半年来，伴随多项首创技术持续推出与工程打磨，公司平均单台算力的 AI Token 生产效率逐月攀升，持续引领行业；高品质 AI Token 日均产量增长超过百倍，并攀升至超万亿量级，年内业务收入已达到去年全年近十倍。 在产业格局上，趋境科技正推动 AI 基础设施从传统算力资源供给向高品质 AI Token 规模化生产与运营升级。依托 ATaaS 平台及 Token 工厂建设运营能力，公司在半年内携手产业伙伴推进十余个日均万亿级 AI Token 工厂项目，推动国产算力规模化应用，联合地方国资、产业龙头及生态伙伴，构建连接算力基础设施、大模型与行业应用的新型 AI Token 供给网络。 区域化基础设施布局 公司以河南、杭州、海南为重点，结合区域资源与产业需求，推进高品质 AI Token 生产与服务网络建设。在河南推进与地方国资联合运营，协同开展 Token 生产、销售与客户消纳；华东区域总部落地杭州钱江世纪城，规划建设万卡级 Token 工厂，服务长三角企业级推理需求；在海南探索地方国资建设、趋境提供平台与运营服务的合作模式。通过因地制宜的建设运营模式，推动算力投入转化为可持续的 Token 供给能力，带动本地运营能力与产业生态发展。 产业生态与共建共营 公司与商汤科技、并行科技、弘信电子、网宿科技、摩尔线程、沐曦股份、天数智芯等企业达成生态合作，推动高品质 AI Token 工厂建设与运营，探索基于国产芯片的高品质 AI Token 生产技术方案，共建自主可控的国产 AI 算力生态。携手商汤推进日均十万亿级 Token 工厂建设，共建产线已具备日均万亿级 Token 的生产与稳定消纳能力；联合并行科技打造日均万亿级 Token 工厂，打通算力基础设施、推理优化、标准化 Token 供给与产业应用全链路；与弘信电子完成其旗下燧弘华创无锡、厦门两大 Token 工厂的技术适配与试点落地；携手网宿科技，结合其全球分布式边缘资源与网络能力，开展推理优化和智能调度协同，提升高品质 AI Token 的生产效率与交付稳定性。 持续释放的技术效率红利，推动业务与资本同步迈入高速增长周期。融资节奏与业绩增长同频，年内多轮交割有序落地，保持平均两月一轮的节奏，单轮募资规模环比持续走高；今年内累计募资总额达24亿人民币，获得国资、产业资本与市场化机构持续重仓。系列融资落地后，股东结构进一步多元成熟，汇聚地方国资、金融资本、头部产业集团与一线市场化机构，为后续区域算力共建、国产异构生态协同、大规模行业交付提供坚实支撑。 顶尖科研与开源筑基 ｜构筑系统级长期工程壁垒 商业化进展背后，是趋境科技在科研、开源工程与企业级生产交付方面的持续积累。 从前沿的技术探索到严苛的工程落地，贯穿始终的是一支兼具学术高度与产业经验的核心团队：公司管理团队由创始人兼 CEO 艾智远博士、总裁兼 CFO 武文洁博士、CTO 陈祥麟等组成，共同推进技术研发、资本协同、产业合作与项目交付；在技术研究层面，郑纬民院士担任首席科学顾问，武永卫教授担任首席科学家，为公司底层技术演进提供学术与技术支持；章明星副教授担任董事，指导技术战略与关键研发工作，推动前沿研究与工程实践衔接。 学术研究之外，趋境科技核心团队长期参与大模型推理开源生态建设，团队牵头发起 KTransformers，并参与 Mooncake 的发起与共建，为相关研究提供了面向不同模型、硬件和负载条件的工程验证环境，也推动团队围绕“全系统异构协同”“以存换算”“虚实同构”等方向持续探索。 从学术研究和开源工程出发，相关技术能力进一步沉淀至 ATaaS 平台，并在 AI Token 工厂的真实业务负载中持续检验。秉持“算力更高效、智能更普惠”的理念，趋境科技以真实需求牵引生产投入，以长期交付检验技术能力，正通过 ATaaS 平台和 AI Token 工厂，输出高品质 AI Token 的标准化生产体系，重塑 AI 推理供给范式，赋能千行百业生产级智能化升级。 趋境科技 CEO 艾智远表示：在算力转化为高质量生产力的赛跑中，真正的稀缺壁垒不是规模，而是单位能效与商用交付能力。过去半年，趋境科技以超十倍速的业务增长证明了“少模型、深优化、高品质”路线的巨大商业潜能。资本的持续加注，是对趋境科技业务交付成绩的肯定。面向未来，趋境科技将依托本轮资金加速产能扩张，深化国产 PD 异构方案落地，以更稳定、更高效、更具成本效率的高品质 AI Token 服务支持客户规模化应用，推动国产异构资源更充分地进入真实生产场景，与产业伙伴共同构建多元、稳定、可持续的 AI 推理供给体系。

evidence_summaries: 10 月 26 日中午消息，2026 观猹大会期间，由小米技术委创新产品团队孵化的开源 AI 硬件 HachimoDock 亮相 —— 这是一台可由用户按个人喜好自由改造的桌面 AI 设备，小巧机身集成了个性化桌宠、语音操控电脑端 Agent、智能家居联动、自定义组件创作等能力。 据介绍， HachimoDock 硬件自制成本约 150 元 。团队希望以此降低 AI 硬件的体验门槛，让它成为大众入门 Vibe Coding 的第一台 AI 硬件，体验用自然语言去“创造”一台万能桌面搭子的乐趣。 这台设备的功能不止于此： 用户说出想法，即可与 AI 协作，现场生成并运行新的组件 。基于这一开放机制，它既可以是快捷语音输入的麦克风、内置万款游戏的小游戏机、收听 FM 电台的小收音机，也可以是查看 AI 任务进展与电脑状态的桌面副屏、联动智能家居的桌面中控…… 更多玩法，留给每位用户亲手创造。 用户可以通过语音直接与桌宠进行互动，它会将用户意图转化为各类任务派发给电脑端 Codex、WorkBuddy 等各类 Agent，例如查资料、整理文件、编写代码等，同时 HachimoDock 屏幕上也会同步展示思考、执行、等待确认等任务状态，并以桌宠的表情、动作、简短提示及声音提醒反馈进展；涉及授权的重要操作，仍由相应客户端完成确认。 HachimoDock 的语音操作还延伸到了家居场景 。通过联动小米 Miloco，用户可以语音发起家居控制，小屏也可切换为家居控制台，呈现设备状态、灯光控制和监控画面等内容，让一台桌面设备同时成为电脑 Agent 和智能家居的交互入口。 目前， HachimoDock 已在 GitHub 公开软件源码 ，并提供硬件物料清单、结构件模型及装配教程，用户可以按照自己的想法随意修改。“我们希望，把定义 HachimoDock 的空间留给每一位使用者，让更多人以较低成本，体验 AI 硬件创作的快乐。”小米技术委创新产品团队负责人表示。

worth_tracking.title: AWS 发布基于 CDK 的 Bedrock 托管知识库 Agentic Retrieval 方案：Agent 跨库路由并经 AgentCore Gateway 返回带引用答案。
worth_tracking.ai_summary: AWS 官方博客发布工程方案：用单个 AWS CDK 应用在 Amazon Bedrock 托管知识库上构建企业级 Agentic Retrieval，由 Agent 在金融与天气两个知识库之间路由、通过 AgentCore Gateway 检索并返回带引用的 grounded 答案。 其核心机制是 AgenticRetrieveStream API 将检索变成多轮规划与迭代检索的服务能力；该 API 与 AgentCore Gateway 的 MCP 工具集成仅在托管知识库上支持，客户自管（DIY）知识库不支持。 方案内置可观测性与评估：两个 CloudWatch 仪表盘覆盖七层遥测，支持按需与持续两类评估；相比 2024 年发布的单次 RAG 方案，新架构为四堆栈、七个跨堆栈边界值，由 CDK 自动推导部署顺序。
worth_tracking.brief: AWS 官方博客发布工程方案：用单个 AWS CDK 应用在 Amazon Bedrock 托管知识库上构建企业级 Agentic Retrieval，由 Agent 在金融与天气两个知识库之间路由、通过 AgentCore Gateway 检索并返回带引用的 grounded 答案。 其核心机制是 AgenticRetrieveStream API 将检索变成多轮规划与迭代检索的服务能力；该 API 与 AgentCore Gateway 的 MCP 工具集成仅在托管知识库上支持，客户自管（DIY）知识库不支持。 方案内置可观测性与评估：两个 CloudWatch 仪表盘覆盖七层遥测，支持按需与持续两类评估；相比 2024 年发布的单次 RAG 方案，新架构为四堆栈、七个跨堆栈边界值，由 CDK 自动推导部署顺序。

worth_tracking.title: 投研Agent两年维护的网页清洗与信源筛选代码，被腾讯元宝搜索接口替代。
worth_tracking.ai_summary: 付费投研简报作者陈万运行Agent两年，一直靠 cleaner.py 清洗网页、sites.yaml 维护 387 个信源网址，最近将这两份文件删除，改用腾讯云升级后的元宝搜索 SearchPro：接口提供权威度 0-5 分级、动态摘要、Freshness 时间筛选和 VR 卡垂直信源，接入方式包括腾讯云标准 API、单一 API Key 认证和 MCP（协议版本 2025-06-18）。 腾讯云方面介绍，元宝搜索内部训练压缩模型，把几千 Token 的网页压缩到约 100 个 Gist Token 缓存，推理成本约省 30%；SearchPro 按量计费为极速版、标准版、旗舰版每千次 14 元、20 元、26 元，旗舰版限企业用户，填写邀请码后每月有 6000 次免费调用额度。 元宝搜索称升级后在内部 50 多个核心产品验证，拥有千亿级融合索引，日增索引约 50 亿，日均调用量数亿次，底层检索平均耗时约 8 毫秒；这些指标对应不同环节，底层检索耗时不等于一次完整请求的响应时间，数据为厂商自述。

evidence_titles: Counterpoint：英伟达引领人形机器人 AI 加速器市场，高通、英特尔、特斯拉、小鹏逐步崛起
evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，根据 Counterpoint Research 最新发布的全球人形机器人追踪报告，预计到 2030 年 ，全球人形机器人 AI 加速器累计出货量将 突破 100 万台 ，2026 至 2030 年期间的 复合年增长率（CAGR）高达 144% 。 在计算架构方面，由于视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型与世界模型逐步融合，GPU 在短期内仍将是人形机器人算力的主流架构。与此同时，AI ASIC（专用集成电路）也在快速崛起，特斯拉、小鹏等垂直整合厂商正将汽车领域的自研芯片技术迁移至人形机器人产品线。 英伟达 凭借从算力芯片、模型到仿真工具的完整全栈生态，目前主导人形机器人 GPU 市场，并与智元机器人、宇树科技、优必选、银河通用、Figure AI、Neura Robotics、Noetix Robotics 等头部本体厂商建立了深度合作。 高通 则凭借异构计算架构切入市场，主打能效优势与更低的物料成本（BoM），目前已与 Neura Robotics、VinMotion、Booster Robotics 以及 Figure AI 达成设计合作，但出货规模与英伟达仍有明显差距。 Counterpoint 首席分析师 Soumen Mandal 表示，人形机器人的算力生态正从 GPU 单极主导转向多种 AI 计算架构共存。随着机器人模型从 VLA 向世界行动模型（WAM）演进，专用算力在更低功耗、更小散热约束与更高能效方面的价值将愈发突出。 Counterpoint 副总监 Ethan Qi 指出， GPU 依然是当前最先进具身模型端侧部署的首选，而以特斯拉为代表的车企将成为 ASIC 架构的核心推动者 。随着下一代可支撑通用人工智能（AGI）工作负载的 AI 加速器在 2027 年后进入量产，市场竞争预计将进一步加剧。 在垂直整合阵营中， 特斯拉与小鹏汽车 依托汽车制造经验、自研芯片、专有 AI 模型以及软硬件全栈布局，有望重塑人形机器人 AI 加速器格局。 国内方面，从 地平线 孵化拆分出的 D-Robotics（地瓜机器人） 已与乐聚机器人、LIMX Dynamics 等厂商达成合作，其推出的 RDK S100 算控一体化开发套件采用“CPU+BPU+MCU”架构，内置基于 Nash 架构、算力达 80 TOPS 的 BPU 神经网络处理单元，正持续强化国内人形机器人算力生态的自主化能力。

worth_tracking.title: AWS 发布 Bedrock 上 OpenAI 模型的 Prompt 缓存实战指南，自测六轮 Agent 工作负载输入成本降约 61%–62%。
worth_tracking.ai_summary: AWS 机器学习博客发布工程指南，介绍在 Amazon Bedrock 上为 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 模型配置 prompt caching，以降低 Agent 每轮重读完整上下文带来的输入成本与延迟。 指南覆盖隐式与显式（prompt_cache_breakpoint）两种缓存模式，静态前缀需达 1,024 token 方可命中，并可用 prompt_cache_key 让新会话与子代理复用共享前缀起点。 作者在六轮工具调用负载上测得：GPT-6 Astra 以隐式缓存运行时输入成本比无缓存低约 62%，显式滚动断点节省约 61%，并注明这些是工作负载结果、需对各自 agent 实测。
worth_tracking.brief: AWS 机器学习博客发布工程指南，介绍在 Amazon Bedrock 上为 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 模型配置 prompt caching，以降低 Agent 每轮重读完整上下文带来的输入成本与延迟。 指南覆盖隐式与显式（prompt_cache_breakpoint）两种缓存模式，静态前缀需达 1,024 token 方可命中，并可用 prompt_cache_key 让新会话与子代理复用共享前缀起点。 作者在六轮工具调用负载上测得：GPT-6 Astra 以隐式缓存运行时输入成本比无缓存低约 62%，显式滚动断点节省约 61%，并注明这些是工作负载结果、需对各自 agent 实测。

worth_tracking.title_zh: AWS 发布 Bedrock 上 OpenAI 模型的 Prompt 缓存实战指南，自测六轮 Agent 工作负载输入成本降约 61%–62%。
worth_tracking.memory_note: 指南推荐的实践是隐式与显式混用：显式标记工具和指令作跨会话共享起点，隐式模式随对话增长自动管理历史缓存；命中前提是前缀文本逐字一致，变量内容需放在断点之后。 62% 与 61% 是单一六轮负载下的厂商自测数据而非独立基准，实际收益取决于会话结构、前缀稳定性与序列化一致性，团队采纳前应复测自身负载。
reading_questions: 在历史不断增长、工具频繁更换的长会话中，隐式缓存的命中率与成本节省还能否接近文中结果？
显式与隐式混用时，断点位置的选择是否会影响模型输出质量或 reasoning 内容？

expert_review.importance: Bedrock 上 OpenAI 模型的 prompt 缓存是影响多轮 Agent 推理成本的关键工程手段，该指南给出可复现配置代码与分模式成本数据，直接影响在此平台上构建 Agent 的开发者选型与计费设计。
expert_review.skepticism: 约 62% 与 61% 的节省来自单一六轮工作负载的厂商自测而非独立基准，缓存命中还依赖 1,024 token 门槛与前缀逐字一致，实际收益需按自身会话结构验证。
watch_points: 缓存命中与未命中 token 的实际计费单价是否与文章假设一致，需对照 Bedrock 官方定价页确认。
prompt_cache_key 跨会话与子代理复用在真实流量下的缓存失效策略和 TTL（示例为 30 分钟）管理。
显式断点随会话增长的手动维护成本，以及工具/MCP 序列化变化对缓存命中率的影响。

evidence_titles: Anthropic 招股书披露：曾因安全顾虑暂停旗舰 AI 模型训练一个多月
evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，Anthropic 在当地时间周一公布的 IPO 招股文件中披露，出于安全方面的顾虑，该公司曾暂停下一代旗舰 AI 模型的训练长达一个多月；另外还有四个 AI 智能体在测试期间突破限制，接入了真实的外部计算机系统。 IT之家注意到，这家 Claude 开发企业在文件的风险提示章节中表示，其推迟了一款全新前沿基础模型的预训练工作，目的是强化防护机制，防止模型权重与知识产权被盗。 这份披露内容展现出，研发能力越来越强的 AI 模型会伴随各类安全难题，部分从业者已经发出警示，这类技术未来有可能脱离人类管控。竞争对手 OpenAI 今年早些时候也曾因为安全问题暂停部分训练工作，当时其模型出现了入侵 Hugging Face 平台的情况。 这些事件说明，突发的安全事故有可能打乱核心模型的开发与上线节奏，而这些模型正是 Anthropic 冲刺备受期待的上市进程、实现业务增长的关键。 Anthropic 警示，训练暂停会造成营收延后，使公司落后于竞争对手。这份文件用大约 94 页篇幅罗列了风险因素。 沙箱逃逸 招股文件还披露了此前未对外公开的安全评估事故：四个 AI 模型脱离测试沙箱环境，访问到现实中的计算机系统，相关会话持续时长在 10 小时至 34 小时之间。 Anthropic 称，在和第三方合作方开展网络安全测试时出现操作失误。按照要求测试环境应当关闭联网权限，但最终环境仍保持着互联网连接。 其中一起事故里，该模型的早期版本持续尝试一项无法完成的评估任务，期间找到一条保存的密码，并利用密码获取了第三方系统的管理员权限。随后它拿到更多凭证、修改系统设置，还访问到个人数据。文件没有写明涉事外部合作方的身份。 Anthropic 表示已经通知所有受影响的相关方，没有发现模型刻意躲避人类监管、或是多个模型互相协同行动的证据。事后公司叫停了部分上线前网络安全评估项目，并暂停风险等级更高的强化学习测试环境。 另外，该公司在当地时间上周日称，Claude 曾绕过付费墙，在没有获得人工授权的情况下调取了美国佐治亚州公开的汇总选票数据。

SpaceX closes $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, Elon Musk says
SpaceX 达成史上最大规模 GPU 融资安排，协议总额约 400 亿美元
evidence_summaries: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.
Elon Musk said in an X post that SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs.

IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，SpaceX 当地时间今日正式公布了其与另类资产管理巨头 Apollo 达成的融资安排。 根据双方间的有约束力承诺，SpaceX 和 Apollo 将签署一份 价值约 400 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,670.98 亿元人民币） 的 GPU 及相关设备主融资租赁协议，具体签署时间预计落在 2026 年内。 这一迄今为止规模最大的 GPU 融资协议 将为 SpaceX 的地面计算建设提供下一代 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 芯片。租赁计划预计将于 2027 年上半年 GPU 及相关设备交付后开始实施。 SpaceX 首席财务官 Bret Johnsen 表示： SpaceX 致力于部署全球最大的计算基础设施。随着对计算能力的需求持续加速增长，我们发现对系统集成基础设施的投资回收期已缩短至不到一年。 此次租赁协议不仅使我们的资金来源更加多元化，还解决了实现增长计划所需资金中相当大的一部分。我们正致力于以创纪录的速度将更多计算能力投入运行，以支持面向企业和消费者的 Grok 服务，并为现有及未来的云服务客户提供支持。 相关阅读： 《 马斯克确认 SpaceX 完成 400 亿美元债务融资，用于购买 GPU 》 《 马斯克唱衰新云厂商：200 余家相关公司面临生存危机 》

Anthropic, PBC submitted its Form S-1 registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission, officially signaling its intent to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the […] Anthropic Files Its S-1. The $2 Trillion Number Isn’t In It. Nolan Pratt Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:05 AM PDT 3 min read ANTH.PVT The most anticipated initial public offering filing in years arrived on October 26, 2026, yet it is legally incapable of stating the one number everyone is quoting. Anthropic, PBC submitted its Form S-1 registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission, officially signaling its intent to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT. While the document provides a granular look at the company's financial architecture, it remains silent on the specific share count and price range that will ultimately define its market debut. This is not an act of evasion, but a standard feature of the regulatory process; the S-1 is a disclosure of business health and risk, not a pre-negotiated price tag. What the filing does provide is a clear view of the company's current financial standing. For the first half of 2026, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion against a net loss of $80.7 billion . For market observers, the headline loss requires careful parsing. The figure is largely driven by an increase in the value of convertible bonds, representing a non-cash mark rather than an operating bleed. By separating these accounting adjustments from the underlying business performance, the filing offers a window into the company's scale that was previously obscured by its private status. The silence regarding the offering price is where the market's speculative machinery currently resides. Because the registration statement has been filed but has not yet become effective, no offers or sales are permitted. The pricing mechanism is a staged evolution. Following a confidential filing on June 1, 2026 , the company is now operating on a ladder of private-market valuations that have escalated rapidly: a Series G round in February 2026 valued the company at roughly $380 billion, followed by a Series H round in May 2026 that reached a post-money valuation of $965 billion. These figures are historical markers, not current pricing. Press expectations, which are not figures disclosed in the filing, have pushed the narrative significantly higher. Bloomberg has reported expectations that the IPO could match or exceed the $1.8 trillion valuation of SpaceX, while CNBC has noted investor sentiment circling the $2 trillion mark, a figure previously floated in September reporting . Reuters has suggested a potential capital raise of up to $100 billion. These projections, often citing a range of 22x to 30x revenue, are external market estimates. They reflect the intense demand for the asset, but they remain entirely detached from the formal S-1 document currently under review by the SEC. Story Continues The process from here is a structured march toward effectiveness. The company has named Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters, though reports mentioning other institutions in the syndicate remain unconfirmed. The next phase involves a period of SEC review and subsequent amendments to the registration statement. It is only through these later amendments that the specific price range will be introduced, typically coinciding with the start of the roadshow marketing process. Press reports indicate that this marketing phase could begin as early as November 9, 2026, with a listing targeted for days before the November US midterms. The current state of the filing provides the necessary transparency for potential investors to evaluate the business. However, the valuation remains a moving target, subject to the ongoing dialogue between the underwriters and the institutional buy-side during the upcoming roadshow. The market is not waiting for a number to be revealed in a static document; it is waiting for the price to be discovered through the mechanics of the offering itself. As the SEC review proceeds, the focus remains on the transition from private-market benchmarks to public-market reality. The filing has brought the company a step closer to a historic offering, but the final valuation will only crystallize when the roadshow concludes and the shares are priced through later amendments to the registration statement. Original | Odaily Planet Daily (@OdailyChina)Author | Sudi Xia @ Odaily Planet DailyOn the evening of October 26, Beijing time, artificial intelligence company Original | Odaily Planet Daily ( @OdailyChina ) Author | Sudi Xia @ Odaily Planet Daily On the evening of October 26, Beijing time, artificial intelligence company Anthropic filed its initial public offering (IPO) application with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). According to Anthropic’s S-1 filing (click to view), the company expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT.” Anthropic secretly submitted its IPO application in June. The prospectus indicates that the number of shares offered, price range, and underwriting discounts are left blank on the cover page; a total of 21 underwriters are involved in this IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as joint lead underwriters. Given that the original document is hundreds of pages long and some of its data differs significantly from the earlier draft exposed by Reuters, Odaily Planet Daily has excerpted the key IPO details for readers to quickly review. Five figures that differ from market-reported data Operating loss of $693 million, not $8.7 billion Since the draft prospectus content was reported by Reuters at the end of September, Chinese media have generally portrayed Anthropic's operating loss for the first half of 2026 as approximately $8.7 billion, while the operating loss line item in the prospectus’s income statement is -$693 million. The $8.7 billion is calculated by subtracting the $72.388 billion fair value change loss from the net loss of $80.748 billion. The prospectus explains this change as: “These changes were primarily due to the increase in the fair value of our outstanding convertible notes, resulting from increases in enterprise value during each period.” The net operating loss narrowed from $2.135 billion in the first half of 2025 to $693 million, a 67.5% decrease. According to the prospectus, revenue during the same period increased 14-fold year-over-year. The following are the primary consolidated income statement data (in millions of U.S. dollars): Cash and short-term investments amount to $131.651 billion. The widely circulated figure of “cash of only $20.28 billion” corresponds to the point in time as of December 31, 2025. The prospectus’s balance sheet has been updated to June 30, 2026: cash and cash equivalents amount to $112.389 billion, short-term investments total $19.262 billion, for a combined total of $131.651 billion. The cash flow statement shows that net cash inflows from financing activities in the first half of 2026 were $110.774 billion, with cash and restricted cash at the end of the period totaling $114.918 billion. The claim of "$518 billion in computing power commitments" is not supported by the document. The previously leaked draft stated, "Anthropic plans to spend $518 billion on cloud computing, computing power, and infrastructure over the next year." However, a full search of the prospectus for "518 billion" and "450 billion" yields no results, and the contract commitment table does not list specific amounts at this preliminary prospectus stage. The contract amounts with each counterparty can be verified individually: Microsoft: at least $44.9 billion, period from November 2026 to May 2033. Google: at least $114.5 billion, period from April 2026 to July 2033. Amazon: at least $110 billion, period from May 2026 to April 2036. SpaceXAI up to $120.5 billion by 2029. Nscale up to $44.6 billion by 2033. Lambda $41.3 billion by 2034. Initial procurement of AMD Helios racks expected to exceed $20 billion. An additional $125 billion to $150 billion in Google TPU purchases is planned, with delivery scheduled between 2028 and 2031. Broadcom assumes equipment leasing obligations of up to $42 billion. Both the Microsoft and Amazon agreements include make-up clauses. The prospectus states that if actual consumption falls below the committed amount, a payment must be made to Google to cover the difference, with such difference settled via a true-up mechanism; the Amazon agreement has the same arrangement. The figures for customer concentration are in the notes to the financial statements. The main text of the prospectus states only that “a significant portion of our revenue comes from a limited number of customers,” but does not provide specific percentages; the exact figures are found in Note F-16: In 2025, Customer A and Customer B each accounted for 12% of revenue, Customer B accounted for 18% in the first half of 2025, Customer C accounted for 43% in 2023, and declined to 11% in the first half of 2026. The same footnote also discloses that revenue generated through the cloud service provider (CSP) channel accounted for 11% of total revenue in 2023, 32% in 2024, 47% in 2025, and rose to 48% in the first half of 2026. The proportion of net accounts receivable generated through the same channel was 42% in 2024, 60% in 2025, and 58% as of June 2026. The prospectus lists dependence on cloud providers as a risk factor: “We rely on a limited number of cloud service providers and suppliers, some of whom have strategic and investment relationships with us and are also our customers. This relationship may create complex situations that could lead to conflicts of interest and adversely affect our ability to secure computing power.” Net income retention rate is 900% The 500% figure cited in the market comes from CFO Krishna Rao’s podcast interview in May 2026. The prospectus discloses that, as of September 30, 2026, the net revenue retention rate (NRR) was approximately 900%. The prospectus also specifies the calculation scope for this metric: “The base period is the three months ending prior to the measurement date, and the numerator is the revenue for the three months ending on the measurement date; customers with revenue below $1 during the base period, as well as Claude Pro and Claude Max fixed-subscription users, are excluded from the calculation.” Run-Rate Revenue: The custom metric in the prospectus differs from ARR. The prospectus defines Run-Rate Revenue in the terminology section as: the annualized estimated value of our revenue-generating activities as of a given measurement date, calculated as the sum of (i) the consumer fees incurred over the past 28 days ending on that measurement date multiplied by 13, and (ii) the total monthly subscription fees as of that measurement date multiplied by 12. The consumption fee is calculated by multiplying the past 28 days by 13, not the industry standard of 12. The specific value of this metric is left blank in the prospectus, disclosed as: "As of October 31, 2026, our Run-Rate Revenue was ___ USD." The risk factors section of the prospectus qualifies this metric as follows: “Therefore, these metrics may not accurately reflect our actual performance or future results. Metrics such as Run-Rate Revenue, net revenue retention rate, number of customers, and Claude success rate are based on numerous assumptions and limitations.” Quarterly revenue growth rate decreased from 132% to 45% The quarterly revenue disclosed in the prospectus is: $4.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, $11.6 billion in the second quarter, and $16.8 billion in the third quarter. The sequential growth rate for the second quarter was 132%, and for the third quarter, it was 45%. Monthly annualized recurring revenue (ARR) trajectory: $9 billion by end of 2025, $30 billion in February 2026, $47 billion in May, $65 billion in July, and $67 billion by end of Q3. The company provided three explanations for the slowdown in growth: competitors such as OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 Astra while lowering prices to compete in the agent market; the company’s own anti-distillation measures resulted in account suspensions and customer attrition; and approximately 5% to 7% of revenue came from model distillation activities, which are expected to decline further in the fourth quarter. The prospectus also discloses a difference in reporting methodology: revenue figures include sales through the cloud platform channel without deducting platform commissions, whereas OpenAI’s disclosed annualized revenue reflects net revenue after deducting commissions, making the two figures not directly comparable. Five types of shares, two types each issuing only 1 share The capital structure disclosed on the prospectus cover page includes five categories: 1 share of Class T common stock, 1 share of Class F common stock, and 0 shares of Class E common stock, as shown below: Class T is held by the Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT). The prospectus describes the trust’s mandate as: “Operating as an independent entity governed by trustees with no financial interest, who possess expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise.” The trust may elect and remove Class T directors, and the Class T directors elected thereby shall constitute a majority of the authorized board seats. Class T common stock has no other voting rights or economic rights. Class F shares will be issued prior to this offering to Founder LLC, composed of seven co-founders, holding 50.1% of the total voting power. Class N common shares have no voting rights and are held by key strategic business partners. Anthropic considers itself a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules. The risk factors section of the prospectus states: “Our capital structure includes several recently designed provisions not commonly found in other companies with multiple-class share structures, which may substantially eliminate the ability of Class A common stockholders to influence significant decisions, including changes in control. Our capital structure will, for the foreseeable future, concentrate voting power in LTBT and Founder LLC, resulting in these entities’ voting rights not being derived from or aligned with their economic interests in the company.” The governance structure section further states: "Therefore, holders of Class A common stock will typically be unable to influence the outcome of any matter submitted to shareholders for a vote or the election of directors, regardless of how they vote—unless a majority of the continuing founders cannot agree on how to vote the Class F common stock." A 50% increase in stock price can trigger additional issuance to the charitable fund. The company has donated 846,840,960 shares of Class N common stock to its wholly owned subsidiary, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, representing 5% of the fully diluted shares as of June 30, 2026. The board has also been authorized to issue additional Class N common stock, up to 2% of the total outstanding shares, unexercised options, unvested RSUs, and other equivalent securities at any time the stock price increases by 50% from the previous price milestone, with the IPO offering price serving as the starting point. This authorization is exercised at the discretion of the board. The seven co-founders have separately pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to charitable purposes. The board currently consists of six members, including the co-founder of Netflix. The list of directors and senior management disclosed in the prospectus (as of September 30, 2026): The company has four committees: Audit, Compensation, Nominating and Governance (NGC), and Security and Risk. evidence_summaries: Bringing fast and capable computer use to everyone

GPT-6.1 Terra It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement. In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use: We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it. Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks. OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News: In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select. Here are the pelicans for the different reasoning levels. This pelican for "max" cost 11.3161 cents and took 4 minutes and 11 seconds: Here's a new comparison grid showing pelicans for every reasoning level of OpenAI's current frontier lineup: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6.1 Terra is priced at $1/million input tokens and $5/million output - almost half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and around 10x the price of GPT-6 Luna. evidence_titles: 腾讯混元同声传译大模型 Hy-SimulMT 开源，响应时间仅 3 秒超人类译员
evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，腾讯混元同声传译大模型 Hy-SimulMT 今日发布并开源，具备低时延、高准确率的特点，支持中英语言之间语音到语音实时翻译 —— 说话人的音频可以实时输入到 Hy-SimulMT 模型中，模型会边听边译，实时给出译文和语音，并支持实时音色克隆，可以高度还原说话人声音和语气。该模型在腾讯 Hy 翻译 App 首发， 免费提供服务体验 。 IT之家从官方介绍获悉，低时延是模型的一大亮点，混元同声传译大模型 Hy-SimulMT 的响应时间 实测在 3 秒左右 ，人类专业译员平均水平在 4-5 秒。测评结果显示，该模型的翻译效果超过了市面上主流的开源同传模型，甚至超过大部分的商用同传 API。 官方称，在业界常用的长音频开源评测集 RealSI 上，Hy-SimulMT 展示出了较好的同传翻译效果，见下图： 横轴里的 StreamLAAL 表示同传翻译的延迟指标，反映的模型输出翻译结果相比输入音频的延迟秒数，越低越好。纵轴表示翻译质量，使用 GPT6.1-Sol 进行打分，越高越好。Hy-SimulMT 能做到延迟最低的情况下，效果达到开源模型最佳，甚至超过大多数商业 API。 在短音频测试集上，Hy-SimulMT 也有较好表现，见下图： 为了更准确评估 Hy-SimulMT 的真实水平，该团队在合规允许范围内，广泛收集了互联网上新出现的中文和英文音频，包含软件 AI、医学、制造能源、自然科学、农业食品、商务管理、法律、教育、文化文旅、体育生活共十个领域， 涉及演讲、访谈、会议等多个场景 。 在这份数据上，该团队不仅测试了 Hy-SimulMT 的效果，也请多位人类同传专家对这些音频进行同声传译。 人类同传专家一共 6 位，其中 3 位拥有 CATTI 一级口译证书，3 位拥有 CATTI 二级口译证书，所有专家都有多年的同传实战经验。测评对 Hy-SimulMT 和人类同传专家的翻译内容在延迟和翻译质量上对比，其中人类同传专家选取的是 3 个人中的最高分，在这次能力定位测评中， Hy-SimulMT 在翻译的质量达到人类同传专家水平（得分更高），速度更快（时延更低） 。 参考 HuggingFace Modelscope Github

evidence_summaries: 高品质 AI Token 成为行业新风向

近日，雷峰网获悉，高品质 AI Token 生产服务商趋境科技（Approaching.AI）完成 B 轮融资，本轮融资金额超13亿人民币；今年内已累计募得24亿人民币。多项核心经营指标在半年内实现超十倍速增长，持续获得产业和资本的高度认可。 本轮融资由浙财创新、萧山资本、工银投资、中关村科学城、星连资本及钱江世纪城共同领投。云创资本、湖南高新纵横、建投华科、申万创新投、中信聚信、珠海科技产业集团、商汤科技、网宿科技、甘肃树帜、常金控、元智未来、清证星竹、小咖资本等跟投，老股东尚势资本继续追投。 这是继今年 7 月完成 A 轮融资后，趋境科技短期内再获大额融资。截至今年10月，趋境科技已在 2026 年连续完成多轮融资。密集的资本跟进背后，既反映出市场对 AI 基础设施赛道长期价值的共识，更源于投资人对趋境科技战略聚焦、技术领先和商业化交付成绩等综合实力的肯定——过去半年，趋境科技不但全面跑通了从技术架构到规模化商业交付的全链路，更是持续引领推理行业的技术演进，以技术创新推动了国产算力的性能大跃升。 本轮募集的资金将重点投向高品质 AI Token 产能扩张、ATaaS（Approaching.AI Token as a Service）平台升级迭代、推理底层技术和新产品的研发，以及商业化合作与交付体系完善等方面。 投资者说 · 浙财创新董事长陈栋 “随着 AI 产业走向规模化应用，推理效率、成本与系统优化能力正成为商业化的重要基础。趋境科技在大模型推理领域具备持续的技术积累和工程交付能力。我们期待与公司长期同行，共同推动高效、普惠的 AI 基础设施建设与规模化应用。” 投资者说 · 萧山资本集团董事长祝利烽 “趋境科技是萧山布局 AI Infra 的标杆项目。早在行业聚焦训练时，公司便前瞻深耕推理赛道。依托清华系团队十余年的技术积累与自研 ATaaS 平台，将算力高效转化为可规模化生产的高品质 AI Token，推动国产算力进入核心生产环节。双方正携手推进万卡级人工智能 Token 工厂建设，加速形成‘芯模联动’产业闭环。萧山资本将以长期资本、耐心资本深度赋能，支持其把高品质 AI Token 工厂能力快速复制，为 AI 产业高质量发展注入持久动力。” 投资者说 · 星连资本创始管理合伙人张鸣晨 “星连资本自2024年天使轮成为股东以来，一路见证趋境科技在技术、产品、服务、战略和商业化等全方位不断创造远超预期的佳绩；更是在不到三年的时间里已经快速跃升为 AI 推理领域耀眼的一流企业。这也是星连资本在过往每一轮都持续大额追加投资的根本原因。我们看好趋境科技从技术与商业验证走向规模化建设和持续运营后的广阔成长空间，也期待陪伴团队持续引领 AI 推理行业的发展。” 从“粗放供给”到“品质服务” ｜高品质 AI Token 成为行业新风向 Token 市场发展初期，行业供给侧多“重 Token 数、轻服务品质”，以粗放扩量的方式快速做大供给规模。彼时大模型尚处在试点验证阶段，未深度嵌入企业核心生产链路，业务对性能、稳定性、模型质量的容错空间较大，这类供给模式得以被市场接纳。而趋境科技自创立之初，便坚持锚定生产级推理标准，持续投入推理系统原始创新，夯实工程底座，在行业内率先定义高品质 AI Token 服务理念。 趋境科技所定义的“高品质 AI Token”：锚定生产级场景，提供高智能、低时延、高速率、强稳定，兼具规模化交付能力与可控综合成本的 AI Token 服务。 伴随产业重心转向 Agent 驱动的业务闭环落地，大模型逐步承载生产级核心流程，AI 推理行业正迎来范式转变：企业对 AI Token 的智能水平、响应时延、输出速度、上下文完整性、服务稳定性提出了严苛的生产级刚性要求。这一转变与趋境一直以来坚持和倡导的高品质AI Token 服务理念不谋而合。 产业拐点显现，Token 市场快速形成清晰的品质分层：“可用即可”的粗放供给已难以匹配生产场景诉求，兼顾多维指标平衡的高品质 AI Token 供给稀缺、需求激增，成为市场刚需。作为高品质 AI Token 服务最早的布局者和深耕者，趋境科技凭借长期沉淀的推理系统底层技术与工程化能力，持续推进高品质 AI Token 服务的规模化交付。趋境科技现已成为高品质 AI Token 服务领域的领航者。 立足“少模型、深优化、高品质” ｜加速高品质 AI Token 规模化交付 高品质 AI Token 能够持续规模化交付，最终取决于两个核心命题：单位算力效能能否持续提升，规模化供给能力能否稳定增长。 围绕这一目标，为兑现高品质 AI Token 的生产标准，趋境坚持“少模型、深优化、高品质”的技术路线，聚焦市场需求明确、应用广泛的主流大模型，持续推进“异构推理”“以存换算”“虚实同构”等多项全球首创技术的工程落地，专注企业生产场景的高品质 AI Token 需求。 “少模型、深优化”解决的是“同一批算力能够生产多少高品质 AI Token”，稳定生产负载和跨集群运营解决的是“这些算力有多少时间真正处于有效工作状态”。“少模型”本身并不天然带来更高的利用率，只有单位算力产出和有效利用率同时提升，AI Token 业务的单位经济才有可能成立。 这一路线背后的商业逻辑非常明确：企业级客户最终为业务结果付费，而不是为模型兼容数量付费。 目前，趋境科技已经形成一套可复制的高品质 AI Token 工厂建设与运营模式：既有日均数万亿级 Token 产能的已投产项目，也有面向区域产业生态与头部客户的战略合作及在建布局。更重要的是，整体业务已经跨过成本线。以真实业绩验证了 ATaaS 平台的大规模交付与持续运营能力。 技术创新重构国产算力体系 ｜性价比超越国际最领先算力 让国产算力能够支撑高品质 AI Token 的生产是趋境科技一直以来的目标。 面对国内外芯片的性能差异，趋境科技探索出一条以系统级技术创新实现算力效率突破的新路径，先后率先提出了“国产 Prefill-Decode（PD）异构协同”“高性能异构 KV Cache 转换”“异构算力计算融合”等一系列创新技术方案，重构国产算力计算模式和推理体系，并已在高标准生产场景中正式投产。 在真实生产级环境中，实现国产芯片承载万亿级头部大模型，并达成高品质 AI Token 规模化生产，同时整体性价比超越国际最领先算力。 趋境首创的异构协同推理技术，在保障模型输出质量、响应速度和服务稳定性的前提下，以更低的硬件投入实现更高的有效 Token 产出，稳定承接头部客户的真实业务需求。 这一突破具备双重开创性价值：在商业层面，构筑差异化核心技术护城河，为趋境规模化共建高品质 AI Token 工厂打开增长天花板，支撑业绩与资本价值持续跃升；在产业战略层面，有助于跳出单纯比拼硬件参数的技术竞争，重新定义国产算力价值标尺，让分散在全国、不同架构的国芯资产释放足额推理产能，为国家搭建自主可控、供给充沛、具备商业经济性的 AI 推理底座提供可落地的核心工程方案，进一步夯实我国大模型产业链安全与算力自主根基。 以技术拓产量 ｜半年实现业绩十倍跃升 持续自主技术创新，是驱动趋境科技高品质 AI Token 产量实现指数级增长的核心动力。 半年来，伴随多项首创技术持续推出与工程打磨，公司平均单台算力的 AI Token 生产效率逐月攀升，持续引领行业；高品质 AI Token 日均产量增长超过百倍，并攀升至超万亿量级，年内业务收入已达到去年全年近十倍。 在产业格局上，趋境科技正推动 AI 基础设施从传统算力资源供给向高品质 AI Token 规模化生产与运营升级。依托 ATaaS 平台及 Token 工厂建设运营能力，公司在半年内携手产业伙伴推进十余个日均万亿级 AI Token 工厂项目，推动国产算力规模化应用，联合地方国资、产业龙头及生态伙伴，构建连接算力基础设施、大模型与行业应用的新型 AI Token 供给网络。 区域化基础设施布局 公司以河南、杭州、海南为重点，结合区域资源与产业需求，推进高品质 AI Token 生产与服务网络建设。在河南推进与地方国资联合运营，协同开展 Token 生产、销售与客户消纳；华东区域总部落地杭州钱江世纪城，规划建设万卡级 Token 工厂，服务长三角企业级推理需求；在海南探索地方国资建设、趋境提供平台与运营服务的合作模式。通过因地制宜的建设运营模式，推动算力投入转化为可持续的 Token 供给能力，带动本地运营能力与产业生态发展。 产业生态与共建共营 公司与商汤科技、并行科技、弘信电子、网宿科技、摩尔线程、沐曦股份、天数智芯等企业达成生态合作，推动高品质 AI Token 工厂建设与运营，探索基于国产芯片的高品质 AI Token 生产技术方案，共建自主可控的国产 AI 算力生态。携手商汤推进日均十万亿级 Token 工厂建设，共建产线已具备日均万亿级 Token 的生产与稳定消纳能力；联合并行科技打造日均万亿级 Token 工厂，打通算力基础设施、推理优化、标准化 Token 供给与产业应用全链路；与弘信电子完成其旗下燧弘华创无锡、厦门两大 Token 工厂的技术适配与试点落地；携手网宿科技，结合其全球分布式边缘资源与网络能力，开展推理优化和智能调度协同，提升高品质 AI Token 的生产效率与交付稳定性。 持续释放的技术效率红利，推动业务与资本同步迈入高速增长周期。融资节奏与业绩增长同频，年内多轮交割有序落地，保持平均两月一轮的节奏，单轮募资规模环比持续走高；今年内累计募资总额达24亿人民币，获得国资、产业资本与市场化机构持续重仓。系列融资落地后，股东结构进一步多元成熟，汇聚地方国资、金融资本、头部产业集团与一线市场化机构，为后续区域算力共建、国产异构生态协同、大规模行业交付提供坚实支撑。 顶尖科研与开源筑基 ｜构筑系统级长期工程壁垒 商业化进展背后，是趋境科技在科研、开源工程与企业级生产交付方面的持续积累。 从前沿的技术探索到严苛的工程落地，贯穿始终的是一支兼具学术高度与产业经验的核心团队：公司管理团队由创始人兼 CEO 艾智远博士、总裁兼 CFO 武文洁博士、CTO 陈祥麟等组成，共同推进技术研发、资本协同、产业合作与项目交付；在技术研究层面，郑纬民院士担任首席科学顾问，武永卫教授担任首席科学家，为公司底层技术演进提供学术与技术支持；章明星副教授担任董事，指导技术战略与关键研发工作，推动前沿研究与工程实践衔接。 学术研究之外，趋境科技核心团队长期参与大模型推理开源生态建设，团队牵头发起 KTransformers，并参与 Mooncake 的发起与共建，为相关研究提供了面向不同模型、硬件和负载条件的工程验证环境，也推动团队围绕“全系统异构协同”“以存换算”“虚实同构”等方向持续探索。 从学术研究和开源工程出发，相关技术能力进一步沉淀至 ATaaS 平台，并在 AI Token 工厂的真实业务负载中持续检验。秉持“算力更高效、智能更普惠”的理念，趋境科技以真实需求牵引生产投入，以长期交付检验技术能力，正通过 ATaaS 平台和 AI Token 工厂，输出高品质 AI Token 的标准化生产体系，重塑 AI 推理供给范式，赋能千行百业生产级智能化升级。 趋境科技 CEO 艾智远表示：在算力转化为高质量生产力的赛跑中，真正的稀缺壁垒不是规模，而是单位能效与商用交付能力。过去半年，趋境科技以超十倍速的业务增长证明了“少模型、深优化、高品质”路线的巨大商业潜能。资本的持续加注，是对趋境科技业务交付成绩的肯定。面向未来，趋境科技将依托本轮资金加速产能扩张，深化国产 PD 异构方案落地，以更稳定、更高效、更具成本效率的高品质 AI Token 服务支持客户规模化应用，推动国产异构资源更充分地进入真实生产场景，与产业伙伴共同构建多元、稳定、可持续的 AI 推理供给体系。

evidence_titles: 小米开源硬件 HachimoDock 亮相，150 元就能复刻万能 AI 桌宠
evidence_summaries: 10 月 26 日中午消息，2026 观猹大会期间，由小米技术委创新产品团队孵化的开源 AI 硬件 HachimoDock 亮相 —— 这是一台可由用户按个人喜好自由改造的桌面 AI 设备，小巧机身集成了个性化桌宠、语音操控电脑端 Agent、智能家居联动、自定义组件创作等能力。 据介绍， HachimoDock 硬件自制成本约 150 元 。团队希望以此降低 AI 硬件的体验门槛，让它成为大众入门 Vibe Coding 的第一台 AI 硬件，体验用自然语言去“创造”一台万能桌面搭子的乐趣。 这台设备的功能不止于此： 用户说出想法，即可与 AI 协作，现场生成并运行新的组件 。基于这一开放机制，它既可以是快捷语音输入的麦克风、内置万款游戏的小游戏机、收听 FM 电台的小收音机，也可以是查看 AI 任务进展与电脑状态的桌面副屏、联动智能家居的桌面中控…… 更多玩法，留给每位用户亲手创造。 用户可以通过语音直接与桌宠进行互动，它会将用户意图转化为各类任务派发给电脑端 Codex、WorkBuddy 等各类 Agent，例如查资料、整理文件、编写代码等，同时 HachimoDock 屏幕上也会同步展示思考、执行、等待确认等任务状态，并以桌宠的表情、动作、简短提示及声音提醒反馈进展；涉及授权的重要操作，仍由相应客户端完成确认。 HachimoDock 的语音操作还延伸到了家居场景 。通过联动小米 Miloco，用户可以语音发起家居控制，小屏也可切换为家居控制台，呈现设备状态、灯光控制和监控画面等内容，让一台桌面设备同时成为电脑 Agent 和智能家居的交互入口。 目前， HachimoDock 已在 GitHub 公开软件源码 ，并提供硬件物料清单、结构件模型及装配教程，用户可以按照自己的想法随意修改。“我们希望，把定义 HachimoDock 的空间留给每一位使用者，让更多人以较低成本，体验 AI 硬件创作的快乐。”小米技术委创新产品团队负责人表示。

technical_progress.title: AWS 发布基于 CDK 的 Bedrock 托管知识库 Agentic Retrieval 方案：Agent 跨库路由并经 AgentCore Gateway 返回带引用答案。
technical_progress.ai_summary: AWS 官方博客发布工程方案：用单个 AWS CDK 应用在 Amazon Bedrock 托管知识库上构建企业级 Agentic Retrieval，由 Agent 在金融与天气两个知识库之间路由、通过 AgentCore Gateway 检索并返回带引用的 grounded 答案。 其核心机制是 AgenticRetrieveStream API 将检索变成多轮规划与迭代检索的服务能力；该 API 与 AgentCore Gateway 的 MCP 工具集成仅在托管知识库上支持，客户自管（DIY）知识库不支持。 方案内置可观测性与评估：两个 CloudWatch 仪表盘覆盖七层遥测，支持按需与持续两类评估；相比 2024 年发布的单次 RAG 方案，新架构为四堆栈、七个跨堆栈边界值，由 CDK 自动推导部署顺序。

technical_progress.title: 投研Agent两年维护的网页清洗与信源筛选代码，被腾讯元宝搜索接口替代。
technical_progress.ai_summary: 付费投研简报作者陈万运行Agent两年，一直靠 cleaner.py 清洗网页、sites.yaml 维护 387 个信源网址，最近将这两份文件删除，改用腾讯云升级后的元宝搜索 SearchPro：接口提供权威度 0-5 分级、动态摘要、Freshness 时间筛选和 VR 卡垂直信源，接入方式包括腾讯云标准 API、单一 API Key 认证和 MCP（协议版本 2025-06-18）。 腾讯云方面介绍，元宝搜索内部训练压缩模型，把几千 Token 的网页压缩到约 100 个 Gist Token 缓存，推理成本约省 30%；SearchPro 按量计费为极速版、标准版、旗舰版每千次 14 元、20 元、26 元，旗舰版限企业用户，填写邀请码后每月有 6000 次免费调用额度。 元宝搜索称升级后在内部 50 多个核心产品验证，拥有千亿级融合索引，日增索引约 50 亿，日均调用量数亿次，底层检索平均耗时约 8 毫秒；这些指标对应不同环节，底层检索耗时不等于一次完整请求的响应时间，数据为厂商自述。

evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，根据 Counterpoint Research 最新发布的全球人形机器人追踪报告，预计到 2030 年 ，全球人形机器人 AI 加速器累计出货量将 突破 100 万台 ，2026 至 2030 年期间的 复合年增长率（CAGR）高达 144% 。 在计算架构方面，由于视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型与世界模型逐步融合，GPU 在短期内仍将是人形机器人算力的主流架构。与此同时，AI ASIC（专用集成电路）也在快速崛起，特斯拉、小鹏等垂直整合厂商正将汽车领域的自研芯片技术迁移至人形机器人产品线。 英伟达 凭借从算力芯片、模型到仿真工具的完整全栈生态，目前主导人形机器人 GPU 市场，并与智元机器人、宇树科技、优必选、银河通用、Figure AI、Neura Robotics、Noetix Robotics 等头部本体厂商建立了深度合作。 高通 则凭借异构计算架构切入市场，主打能效优势与更低的物料成本（BoM），目前已与 Neura Robotics、VinMotion、Booster Robotics 以及 Figure AI 达成设计合作，但出货规模与英伟达仍有明显差距。 Counterpoint 首席分析师 Soumen Mandal 表示，人形机器人的算力生态正从 GPU 单极主导转向多种 AI 计算架构共存。随着机器人模型从 VLA 向世界行动模型（WAM）演进，专用算力在更低功耗、更小散热约束与更高能效方面的价值将愈发突出。 Counterpoint 副总监 Ethan Qi 指出， GPU 依然是当前最先进具身模型端侧部署的首选，而以特斯拉为代表的车企将成为 ASIC 架构的核心推动者 。随着下一代可支撑通用人工智能（AGI）工作负载的 AI 加速器在 2027 年后进入量产，市场竞争预计将进一步加剧。 在垂直整合阵营中， 特斯拉与小鹏汽车 依托汽车制造经验、自研芯片、专有 AI 模型以及软硬件全栈布局，有望重塑人形机器人 AI 加速器格局。 国内方面，从 地平线 孵化拆分出的 D-Robotics（地瓜机器人） 已与乐聚机器人、LIMX Dynamics 等厂商达成合作，其推出的 RDK S100 算控一体化开发套件采用“CPU+BPU+MCU”架构，内置基于 Nash 架构、算力达 80 TOPS 的 BPU 神经网络处理单元，正持续强化国内人形机器人算力生态的自主化能力。

technical_progress.title_zh: Counterpoint：预计2030年人形机器人AI加速器累计出货破100万台，英伟达当前主导GPU市场。
technical_progress.memory_note: 本条为Counterpoint市场追踪报告：100万台与144% CAGR系机构出货预测，英伟达“主导”与高通“出货规模仍有明显差距”也是报告判断，而非厂商官方销售数据，报道未披露份额口径。 “2027年后量产”的下一代可支撑AGI工作负载的AI加速器属于Counterpoint预期，尚无可核验的厂商产品与时间表，需与后续厂商公告对照观察。

technical_progress.title: AWS 发布 Bedrock 上 OpenAI 模型的 Prompt 缓存实战指南，自测六轮 Agent 工作负载输入成本降约 61%–62%。
technical_progress.ai_summary: AWS 机器学习博客发布工程指南，介绍在 Amazon Bedrock 上为 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 模型配置 prompt caching，以降低 Agent 每轮重读完整上下文带来的输入成本与延迟。 指南覆盖隐式与显式（prompt_cache_breakpoint）两种缓存模式，静态前缀需达 1,024 token 方可命中，并可用 prompt_cache_key 让新会话与子代理复用共享前缀起点。 作者在六轮工具调用负载上测得：GPT-6 Astra 以隐式缓存运行时输入成本比无缓存低约 62%，显式滚动断点节省约 61%，并注明这些是工作负载结果、需对各自 agent 实测。
technical_progress.brief: AWS 机器学习博客发布工程指南，介绍在 Amazon Bedrock 上为 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 模型配置 prompt caching，以降低 Agent 每轮重读完整上下文带来的输入成本与延迟。 指南覆盖隐式与显式（prompt_cache_breakpoint）两种缓存模式，静态前缀需达 1,024 token 方可命中，并可用 prompt_cache_key 让新会话与子代理复用共享前缀起点。 作者在六轮工具调用负载上测得：GPT-6 Astra 以隐式缓存运行时输入成本比无缓存低约 62%，显式滚动断点节省约 61%，并注明这些是工作负载结果、需对各自 agent 实测。
evidence_titles: Groundhog Day for AI agents: Prompt caching patterns for using OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock
evidence_summaries: Every time an agent takes a step, it re-reads its entire context before acting. Here is how prompt caching for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock lets your agent remember, cutting input cost and latency without resending the same tools, instructions, and history every turn.

technical_progress.title_zh: AWS 发布 Bedrock 上 OpenAI 模型的 Prompt 缓存实战指南，自测六轮 Agent 工作负载输入成本降约 61%–62%。
technical_progress.memory_note: 指南推荐的实践是隐式与显式混用：显式标记工具和指令作跨会话共享起点，隐式模式随对话增长自动管理历史缓存；命中前提是前缀文本逐字一致，变量内容需放在断点之后。 62% 与 61% 是单一六轮负载下的厂商自测数据而非独立基准，实际收益取决于会话结构、前缀稳定性与序列化一致性，团队采纳前应复测自身负载。
reading_questions: 在历史不断增长、工具频繁更换的长会话中，隐式缓存的命中率与成本节省还能否接近文中结果？
显式与隐式混用时，断点位置的选择是否会影响模型输出质量或 reasoning 内容？

expert_review.importance: Bedrock 上 OpenAI 模型的 prompt 缓存是影响多轮 Agent 推理成本的关键工程手段，该指南给出可复现配置代码与分模式成本数据，直接影响在此平台上构建 Agent 的开发者选型与计费设计。
expert_review.skepticism: 约 62% 与 61% 的节省来自单一六轮工作负载的厂商自测而非独立基准，缓存命中还依赖 1,024 token 门槛与前缀逐字一致，实际收益需按自身会话结构验证。
watch_points: 缓存命中与未命中 token 的实际计费单价是否与文章假设一致，需对照 Bedrock 官方定价页确认。
prompt_cache_key 跨会话与子代理复用在真实流量下的缓存失效策略和 TTL（示例为 30 分钟）管理。
显式断点随会话增长的手动维护成本，以及工具/MCP 序列化变化对缓存命中率的影响。

evidence_titles: Anthropic 招股书披露：曾因安全顾虑暂停旗舰 AI 模型训练一个多月
evidence_summaries: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，Anthropic 在当地时间周一公布的 IPO 招股文件中披露，出于安全方面的顾虑，该公司曾暂停下一代旗舰 AI 模型的训练长达一个多月；另外还有四个 AI 智能体在测试期间突破限制，接入了真实的外部计算机系统。 IT之家注意到，这家 Claude 开发企业在文件的风险提示章节中表示，其推迟了一款全新前沿基础模型的预训练工作，目的是强化防护机制，防止模型权重与知识产权被盗。 这份披露内容展现出，研发能力越来越强的 AI 模型会伴随各类安全难题，部分从业者已经发出警示，这类技术未来有可能脱离人类管控。竞争对手 OpenAI 今年早些时候也曾因为安全问题暂停部分训练工作，当时其模型出现了入侵 Hugging Face 平台的情况。 这些事件说明，突发的安全事故有可能打乱核心模型的开发与上线节奏，而这些模型正是 Anthropic 冲刺备受期待的上市进程、实现业务增长的关键。 Anthropic 警示，训练暂停会造成营收延后，使公司落后于竞争对手。这份文件用大约 94 页篇幅罗列了风险因素。 沙箱逃逸 招股文件还披露了此前未对外公开的安全评估事故：四个 AI 模型脱离测试沙箱环境，访问到现实中的计算机系统，相关会话持续时长在 10 小时至 34 小时之间。 Anthropic 称，在和第三方合作方开展网络安全测试时出现操作失误。按照要求测试环境应当关闭联网权限，但最终环境仍保持着互联网连接。 其中一起事故里，该模型的早期版本持续尝试一项无法完成的评估任务，期间找到一条保存的密码，并利用密码获取了第三方系统的管理员权限。随后它拿到更多凭证、修改系统设置，还访问到个人数据。文件没有写明涉事外部合作方的身份。 Anthropic 表示已经通知所有受影响的相关方，没有发现模型刻意躲避人类监管、或是多个模型互相协同行动的证据。事后公司叫停了部分上线前网络安全评估项目，并暂停风险等级更高的强化学习测试环境。 另外，该公司在当地时间上周日称，Claude 曾绕过付费墙，在没有获得人工授权的情况下调取了美国佐治亚州公开的汇总选票数据。

items.ai_summary: SpaceX 已公开披露与 Apollo 管理实体达成约 400 亿美元的约束性 GPU 融资承诺，用于采购 GPU 及相关数据中心设备。 根据安排，Apollo 旗下实体将购买芯片和服务器硬件，再以约 5 年期租赁形式提供给 SpaceX，租赁预计在 2027 年上半年设备交付后开始。 SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen 表示公司在 AI 基础设施投资上已看到不到一年的投资回收期，该租赁协议将多元化资金来源并支持 Grok 及云服务扩张。

evidence_summaries: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.
Elon Musk said in an X post that SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs.

IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，SpaceX 当地时间今日正式公布了其与另类资产管理巨头 Apollo 达成的融资安排。 根据双方间的有约束力承诺，SpaceX 和 Apollo 将签署一份 价值约 400 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,670.98 亿元人民币） 的 GPU 及相关设备主融资租赁协议，具体签署时间预计落在 2026 年内。 这一迄今为止规模最大的 GPU 融资协议 将为 SpaceX 的地面计算建设提供下一代 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 芯片。租赁计划预计将于 2027 年上半年 GPU 及相关设备交付后开始实施。 SpaceX 首席财务官 Bret Johnsen 表示： SpaceX 致力于部署全球最大的计算基础设施。随着对计算能力的需求持续加速增长，我们发现对系统集成基础设施的投资回收期已缩短至不到一年。 此次租赁协议不仅使我们的资金来源更加多元化，还解决了实现增长计划所需资金中相当大的一部分。我们正致力于以创纪录的速度将更多计算能力投入运行，以支持面向企业和消费者的 Grok 服务，并为现有及未来的云服务客户提供支持。 相关阅读： 《 马斯克确认 SpaceX 完成 400 亿美元债务融资，用于购买 GPU 》 《 马斯克唱衰新云厂商：200 余家相关公司面临生存危机 》

The most anticipated initial public offering filing in years arrived on October 26, 2026, yet it is legally incapable of stating the one number everyone is quoting. Anthropic, PBC submitted its Form S-1 registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission, officially signaling its intent to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the […] Anthropic Files Its S-1. The $2 Trillion Number Isn’t In It. Nolan Pratt Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:05 AM PDT 3 min read ANTH.PVT The most anticipated initial public offering filing in years arrived on October 26, 2026, yet it is legally incapable of stating the one number everyone is quoting. Anthropic, PBC submitted its Form S-1 registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission, officially signaling its intent to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT. While the document provides a granular look at the company's financial architecture, it remains silent on the specific share count and price range that will ultimately define its market debut. This is not an act of evasion, but a standard feature of the regulatory process; the S-1 is a disclosure of business health and risk, not a pre-negotiated price tag. What the filing does provide is a clear view of the company's current financial standing. For the first half of 2026, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion against a net loss of $80.7 billion . For market observers, the headline loss requires careful parsing. The figure is largely driven by an increase in the value of convertible bonds, representing a non-cash mark rather than an operating bleed. By separating these accounting adjustments from the underlying business performance, the filing offers a window into the company's scale that was previously obscured by its private status. The silence regarding the offering price is where the market's speculative machinery currently resides. Because the registration statement has been filed but has not yet become effective, no offers or sales are permitted. The pricing mechanism is a staged evolution. Following a confidential filing on June 1, 2026 , the company is now operating on a ladder of private-market valuations that have escalated rapidly: a Series G round in February 2026 valued the company at roughly $380 billion, followed by a Series H round in May 2026 that reached a post-money valuation of $965 billion. These figures are historical markers, not current pricing. Press expectations, which are not figures disclosed in the filing, have pushed the narrative significantly higher. Bloomberg has reported expectations that the IPO could match or exceed the $1.8 trillion valuation of SpaceX, while CNBC has noted investor sentiment circling the $2 trillion mark, a figure previously floated in September reporting . Reuters has suggested a potential capital raise of up to $100 billion. These projections, often citing a range of 22x to 30x revenue, are external market estimates. They reflect the intense demand for the asset, but they remain entirely detached from the formal S-1 document currently under review by the SEC. Story Continues The process from here is a structured march toward effectiveness. The company has named Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters, though reports mentioning other institutions in the syndicate remain unconfirmed. Original | Odaily Planet Daily (@OdailyChina)Author | Sudi Xia @ Odaily Planet DailyOn the evening of October 26, Beijing time, artificial intelligence company Original | Odaily Planet Daily ( @OdailyChina ) Author | Sudi Xia @ Odaily Planet Daily On the evening of October 26, Beijing time, artificial intelligence company Anthropic filed its initial public offering (IPO) application with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). According to Anthropic’s S-1 filing (click to view), the company expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT.” Anthropic secretly submitted its IPO application in June. The prospectus indicates that the number of shares offered, price range, and underwriting discounts are left blank on the cover page; a total of 21 underwriters are involved in this IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as joint lead underwriters. Given that the original document is hundreds of pages long and some of its data differs significantly from the earlier draft exposed by Reuters, Odaily Planet Daily has excerpted the key IPO details for readers to quickly review. Five figures that differ from market-reported data Operating loss of $693 million, not $8.7 billion Since the draft prospectus content was reported by Reuters at the end of September, Chinese media have generally portrayed Anthropic's operating loss for the first half of 2026 as approximately $8.7 billion, while the operating loss line item in the prospectus’s income statement is -$693 million. The $8.7 billion is calculated by subtracting the $72.388 billion fair value change loss from the net loss of $80.748 billion. The prospectus explains this change as: “These changes were primarily due to the increase in the fair value of our outstanding convertible notes, resulting from increases in enterprise value during each period.” The net operating loss narrowed from $2.135 billion in the first half of 2025 to $693 million, a 67.5% decrease. According to the prospectus, revenue during the same period increased 14-fold year-over-year. The following are the primary consolidated income statement data (in millions of U.S. dollars): Cash and short-term investments amount to $131.651 billion. The widely circulated figure of “cash of only $20.28 billion” corresponds to the point in time as of December 31, 2025. The prospectus’s balance sheet has been updated to June 30, 2026: cash and cash equivalents amount to $112.389 billion, short-term investments total $19.262 billion, for a combined total of $131.651 billion. The cash flow statement shows that net cash inflows from financing activities in the first half of 2026 were $110.774 billion, with cash and restricted cash at the end of the period totaling $114.918 billion. The claim of "$518 billion in computing power commitments" is not supported by the document. The previously leaked draft stated, "Anthropic plans to spend $518 billion on cloud computing, computing power, and infrastructure over the next year." However, a full search of the prospectus for "518 billion" and "450 billion" yields no results, and the contract commitment table does not list specific amounts at this preliminary prospectus stage. The contract amounts with each counterparty can be verified individually: Microsoft: at least $44.9 billion, period from November 2026 to May 2033. Google: at least $114.5 billion, period from April 2026 to July 2033. Amazon: at least $110 billion, period from May 2026 to April 2036. SpaceXAI up to $120.5 billion by 2029. Nscale up to $44.6 billion by 2033. Lambda $41.3 billion by 2034. Initial procurement of AMD Helios racks expected to exceed $20 billion. An additional $125 billion to $150 billion in Google TPU purchases is planned, with delivery scheduled between 2028 and 2031. Broadcom assumes equipment leasing obligations of up to $42 billion. Both the Microsoft and Amazon agreements include make-up clauses. The prospectus states that if actual consumption falls below the committed amount, a payment must be made to Google to cover the difference, with such difference settled via a true-up mechanism; the Amazon agreement has the same arrangement. The figures for customer concentration are in the notes to the financial statements. The main text of the prospectus states only that “a significant portion of our revenue comes from a limited number of customers,” but does not provide specific percentages; the exact figures are found in Note F-16: In 2025, Customer A and Customer B each accounted for 12% of revenue, Customer B accounted for 18% in the first half of 2025, Customer C accounted for 43% in 2023, and declined to 11% in the first half of 2026. The same footnote also discloses that revenue generated through the cloud service provider (CSP) channel accounted for 11% of total revenue in 2023, 32% in 2024, 47% in 2025, and rose to 48% in the first half of 2026. The proportion of net accounts receivable generated through the same channel was 42% in 2024, 60% in 2025, and 58% as of June 2026. The prospectus lists dependence on cloud providers as a risk factor: “We rely on a limited number of cloud service providers and suppliers, some of whom have strategic and investment relationships with us and are also our customers. This relationship may create complex situations that could lead to conflicts of interest and adversely affect our ability to secure computing power.” Net income retention rate is 900% The 500% figure cited in the market comes from CFO Krishna Rao’s podcast interview in May 2026. The prospectus discloses that, as of September 30, 2026, the net revenue retention rate (NRR) was approximately 900%. The prospectus also specifies the calculation scope for this metric: “The base period is the three months ending prior to the measurement date, and the numerator is the revenue for the three months ending on the measurement date; customers with revenue below $1 during the base period, as well as Claude Pro and Claude Max fixed-subscription users, are excluded from the calculation.” Run-Rate Revenue: The custom metric in the prospectus differs from ARR. The prospectus defines Run-Rate Revenue in the terminology section as: the annualized estimated value of our revenue-generating activities as of a given measurement date, calculated as the sum of (i) the consumer fees incurred over the past 28 days ending on that measurement date multiplied by 13, and (ii) the total monthly subscription fees as of that measurement date multiplied by 12. The consumption fee is calculated by multiplying the past 28 days by 13, not the industry standard of 12. The specific value of this metric is left blank in the prospectus, disclosed as: "As of October 31, 2026, our Run-Rate Revenue was ___ USD." The risk factors section of the prospectus qualifies this metric as follows: “Therefore, these metrics may not accurately reflect our actual performance or future results. Metrics such as Run-Rate Revenue, net revenue retention rate, number of customers, and Claude success rate are based on numerous assumptions and limitations.” Quarterly revenue growth rate decreased from 132% to 45% The quarterly revenue disclosed in the prospectus is: $4.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, $11.6 billion in the second quarter, and $16.8 billion in the third quarter. The sequential growth rate for the second quarter was 132%, and for the third quarter, it was 45%. Monthly annualized recurring revenue (ARR) trajectory: $9 billion by end of 2025, $30 billion in February 2026, $47 billion in May, $65 billion in July, and $67 billion by end of Q3. The company provided three explanations for the slowdown in growth: competitors such as OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 Astra while lowering prices to compete in the agent market; the company’s own anti-distillation measures resulted in account suspensions and customer attrition; and approximately 5% to 7% of revenue came from model distillation activities, which are expected to decline further in the fourth quarter. The prospectus also discloses a difference in reporting methodology: revenue figures include sales through the cloud platform channel without deducting platform commissions, whereas OpenAI’s disclosed annualized revenue reflects net revenue after deducting commissions, making the two figures not directly comparable. Five types of shares, two types each issuing only 1 share The capital structure disclosed on the prospectus cover page includes five categories: 1 share of Class T common stock, 1 share of Class F common stock, and 0 shares of Class E common stock, as shown below: Class T is held by the Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT). The prospectus describes the trust’s mandate as: “Operating as an independent entity governed by trustees with no financial interest, who possess expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise.” The trust may elect and remove Class T directors, and the Class T directors elected thereby shall constitute a majority of the authorized board seats. Class T common stock has no other voting rights or economic rights. Class F shares will be issued prior to this offering to Founder LLC, composed of seven co-founders, holding 50.1% of the total voting power. Class N common shares have no voting rights and are held by key strategic business partners. Anthropic considers itself a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules. The risk factors section of the prospectus states: “Our capital structure includes several recently designed provisions not commonly found in other companies with multiple-class share structures, which may substantially eliminate the ability of Class A common stockholders to influence significant decisions, including changes in control. Our capital structure will, for the foreseeable future, concentrate voting power in LTBT and Founder LLC, resulting in these entities’ voting rights not being derived from or aligned with their economic interests in the company.” The governance structure section further states: "Therefore, holders of Class A common stock will typically be unable to influence the outcome of any matter submitted to shareholders for a vote or the election of directors, regardless of how they vote—unless a majority of the continuing founders cannot agree on how to vote the Class F common stock." A 50% increase in stock price can trigger additional issuance to the charitable fund. The company has donated 846,840,960 shares of Class N common stock to its wholly owned subsidiary, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, representing 5% of the fully diluted shares as of June 30, 2026. The board has also been authorized to issue additional Class N common stock, up to 2% of the total outstanding shares, unexercised options, unvested RSUs, and other equivalent securities at any time the stock price increases by 50% from the previous price milestone, with the IPO offering price serving as the starting point. This authorization is exercised at the discretion of the board. The seven co-founders have separately pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to charitable purposes. The board currently consists of six members, including the co-founder of Netflix. The list of directors and senior management disclosed in the prospectus (as of September 30, 2026): The company has four committees: Audit, Compensation, Nominating and Governance (NGC), and Security and Risk. The Audit and Compensation committees are composed entirely of independent directors. Jay Kreps resigned as a director in May 2026, Christopher Liddell joined in February 2026, and Vas Narasimhan joined in April 2026. The five co-founders are the selling shareholders in this offering. items.title: OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.1 Terra 模型，主打视觉推理与计算机使用，定价为 $1/$5 每百万 tokens。
items.ai_summary: OpenAI 于 10 月 26 日宣布推出 GPT-6.1 Terra 模型，强调其在详细视觉推理和精确计算机使用方面的能力，同时具备更清晰自然的写作风格。 该模型被定位为产品线中的中端选项，类似 Anthropic 的 Sonnet，在技术沟通上优于 Astra 和 Sol，视觉与计算机使用能力相似但速度更快，而在其他大多数任务上稍弱。 GPT-6.1 Terra 的 API 价格为每百万输入 tokens 1 美元、每百万输出 tokens 5 美元，约为 GPT-5.6 Terra 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 的一半，是 GPT-6 Luna 的约 10 倍。
